questions_and_answers.question_text: What does zhǐ yào mean, and in what pattern is it used?
What does lái indicate in commands and suggestions?
How is lái translated when talking about one's own intention?
Write the Chinese for "Let me take a look."
Write the Chinese for "As long as you do well in your studies, you won't have any trouble finding a job."

answers.answer_text: Nǐ zhǐ yào bǎ shū niànhǎole, zhǎo gōngzuò jiù méiyou wèntí le.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "Let's discuss this question."
Can lái usually be translated in commands?
Write the Chinese for "As long as you help out, we'll be able to do it."

answers.answer_text: Zhǐ yào nǐ lái bāng máng wǒmen jiù yǒu bànfǎ.

articles.text:
7. A: Zhǐ yào nǐ lái bāng máng       As long as you help out, we'll be able
      wǒmen jiù yǒu bànfǎ.           to do it.
   B: Zhè yǒu shénme? Yīnggāide ma! This is nothing. It's only right!

Notes on No. 7

zhǐ yào: "as long as, provided that." This is used in the pattern ZHǏ YÀO...JIÙ....

Bú yào kǎolǜ tài duō, zhǐ yào nǐ Don't think it over so much. If you
xǐhuan jiù hǎo le.               like it, that's all that matters.
Zhǐ yào wǒ jīntian wǎnshang yǒu  As long as I have time tonight, I can
kòng, jiù kěyi bǎ zhèiběn shū    finish reading this book.
kànwán.
Nǐ zhǐ yào bǎ shū niànhǎole,     As long as you do well in your studies,
zhǎo gōngzuò jiù méiyou wèntí le. you won't have any trouble finding
                                 a job.

lái: In COMMANDS and SUGGESTIONS, this verb merely indicates that a person WILL PERFORM SOME ACTION, and can usually go UNTRANSLATED. When talking about one's own intention, lái can be translated as "LET ME" or "LET'S."

Wǒ lái wèn ni.                   Let me ask you.
Wǒmen lái tántan zhèige wèntí.   Let's discuss this question.
Wǒ lái kànkan.                   Let me take a look.
Nǐ kuài qù máng ba! Wǒmen lái    You go take care of what you have to
shōushi.                         do. We'll straighten up.
Lǐ Zhènhàn, qǐng nǐ lái niàn.    Lǐ Zhènhàn, would you read aloud
                                 please?

yīnggāide: This is SHORT for Wǒ bāngzhu nǐ shi yīnggāide, "It is right that I help you." Use yīnggāide to RESPOND when someone thanks you for doing a favor which you consider NATURAL under the circumstances.
